findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's long-lived credentials yields full control over compute, storage and serverless resources, enabling data exfiltration, destruction, and lateral movement.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a highly privileged service user instead of an IAM role with temporary STS credentials, and because no pgp_key is supplied the secret is persisted in cleartext in the Terraform state file, exposing it to anyone who can read state (CI artifacts, S3 backend, local files).

findings.issue_category: Privileged user without MFA or permissions boundary
findings.description: The IAM user carries wide-reaching inline permissions with no permissions boundary and no MFA enforcement, so possession of the static access key alone grants full access with no second factor or blast-radius limit.

The output svc_deploy_key_material publishes the access key material and is not marked sensitive, so it is rendered to console/CI logs and stored in plaintext in state, leaking the credential to anyone with log or state access.
